title: Strings compare and sort by UTF-8 bytes; `false` before `true`
verdict: code point order (UTF8_BINARY), not Java's UTF-16 order; booleans `false < true`
description: Under the default collation (`UTF8_BINARY`) Spark compares strings by their UTF-8 bytes, unsigned, which is code point order: `''` < `U+0000` < `B` < `Z` < `a` < `ab` < `b` < `é` < `z` < `U+FFFF` < `U+10000` < `U+1F600`. A supplementary character sorts above `U+FFFF`, where Java's `String.compareTo` (UTF-16 units) would put it below. `<`, `BETWEEN`, `greatest`, `least` and `ORDER BY` agree, in both ANSI modes.
Booleans order `false` before `true` (`false < true`, `greatest(false, true)` is `true`). NULL placement is spark-null-order's.
reference: Strings in code point order (Lean's `String` order); booleans `false < true` (#1492). `SparkDialect.orders_text` writes them natively.

provenance.checked_by: #2540 S5 probe (session types-casts-caff57), pyspark 4.3.0, Java 21.0.13, macOS arm64, local[1]

evidence.sql: SELECT s FROM VALUES (''), ('\u0000'), ('B'), ('Z'), ('a'), ('ab'), ('b'), ('é'), ('z'), ('\uffff'), ('\U00010000'), ('\U0001F600'), (NULL) AS t(s) ORDER BY s ASC NULLS LAST
evidence.observed: the values in Python's code point order, then NULL; ansi on and off

evidence.sql: SELECT a.s, b.s FROM VALUES <the 12 values and NULL> AS a(s), VALUES <the same> AS b(s) WHERE a.s < b.s
evidence.observed: 66 pairs, exactly those with a < b in code point order; ansi on and off

evidence.sql: SELECT false < true, true < false, greatest(false, true), least(false, true)
